findings.claim: The objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; coordinate contrasts are proxies, not affinity labels.

The learning/control support is the score-clock window [0.0, 0.5] with 50 observed score nodes at 0.01 spacing; curve support is [0.0, 0.49], so no extrapolation beyond the observed nodes is licensed.

The landmark_00_soft_mass curve is non-monotone over the observed window: it rises from about -0.37 z at t=0 to a peak near +1.64 z around t=0.16, then declines to about -0.28 z at t=0.49, with 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict.

Across all 20 landmark soft-mass features, whole-window z is small (|z| < 0.65) while first-rate and last-rate z values are large and frequently opposite in sign, indicating strong within-window rate changes rather than a stable monotone drift.

No soft-mass feature has an accepted polynomial representation (polynomial_accepted=false for all 20), and relative node RMSE is large (0.29-0.99), so a single smooth global trend is not supported for these coordinates.
Each soft-mass trend row is supported by 14 independent batches, so the reported rates are batch-level summaries rather than single-lineage observations.

hypotheses.direction: stage-dependent relevance; no absolute coordinate target asserted
hypotheses.falsifier: If a fixed (non-staged) coordinate relevance reproduces the same endpoint affinity and validity/strain outcomes as the staged variant at matched dose, the stage-dependence hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass continuous curve over the observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: The landmark_00_soft_mass coordinate shows a time-dependent contrast whose rate changes sign within the observed window (rise then decline), so a stage-dependent rather than constant coordinate relevance may merit testing at fixed dose.

hypotheses.direction: retain gradual change; do not introduce a data-derived knot
hypotheses.falsifier: If an independently stable profile yields an accepted polynomial with small relative node RMSE, a data-derived knot would become defensible.
hypotheses.statement: Because landmark_00_soft_mass has no accepted polynomial and large relative node RMSE, a single smooth global coordinate trend is not supported; any staged schedule should be treated as an experimental hypothesis rather than a data-derived knot.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; only continuous curves and trend tables were inspected.
Only soft-mass features were read as curves in this pass; local covariance and displacement coordinate features were not read.
The observed contrasts are coordinate proxies in predicted endpoint world coordinates; they are not affinity labels and no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is asserted.
Selection preference and descendant survival are not established here; no final-affinity benefit is claimed from these coordinate trends.
No absolute coordinate target or spatial gradient is inferred from the contrast curves.
